correctness.rationale: Pairwise envy-freeness with identical valuations forces every effective utility to W/n, giving exact cap q+b_i. Packing all h-valued goods uses sum floor(c_i/h) slots and the unit goods then fit iff sum c_i>=W. The aggregate-budget minimum follows from each extra h slot costing at least h-s budget and a construction that spreads Delta<n initial increments. Exact independent assignment enumeration checked 11,232 instances, reserve minimization over 725 budget levels, and 480 Bernoulli-budget parameter families. Experiments are supplemental to the infinite proof.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Two-denomination fair allocation is equivalent to packing h- and unit-valued goods into the integer payment ceilings q+b_i. The floor capacities for h goods and total capacity are necessary and jointly sufficient. General subsidy/equitability formulations do not encode individual cash limits; a standard general bin-packing representation alone does not state this exact threshold or the reserve minimum. Such an elementary packing equivalence could nevertheless have appeared elsewhere.

originality.rationale: The 2025/2026 individual-payment papers establish the equal-utility premise and decision methods for fixed good types. The new statement is the two-denomination exact floor-capacity characterization, its sharp total-liquidity minimum and its explicit random unit-budget phase law; neither was located in inspected source sections or targeted published research-record searches. General algorithms cover this input class but do not provide the closed-form quantitative statements. This is best-knowledge originality, with unindexed bin-packing equivalence as a real residual risk.

value.rationale: A complete all-population classification and constructive linear-arithmetic algorithm replaces a fixed-types dynamic program on a natural cash-constrained symmetric fair-division subclass. The exact minimum sum of individual cash budgets demonstrates a possibly large indivisibility premium even when total value is divisible by population, and an exact binomial reserve-reliability threshold exposes the residue-class phase transition. Examples distinguish equal total budgets with opposite feasibility; these quantities are directly useful for liquidity planning rather than arbitrary parameter slices. The elementary proof is a feature of the two-denomination structure, not an assertion of general difficulty.
